models.purpose: Represent the real checkpoint and find its bottlenecks.
models.summary: Each check point is its own M/G/1 queue. Regular and pre-check passengers stay separate, and each ID queue feeds four screening queues. Arrival rates fitted in Mathematica are 4.63476 and 6.52921 per minute. A suspicious passenger appears with probability 1/1000 and blocks a queue for 10 minutes. Three bottlenecks: too few pre-check ID points, exclusive screening assignment, suspicious passengers.

models.purpose: Route passengers to raise throughput toward the tandem ceiling.
models.summary: A Lyapunov function sums the squared backlogs. Each slot the algorithm sends flow over the link with the largest positive differential backlog, and never against a negative one. Pre-check passengers may use regular points but then take regular service time. Throughput reaches 7.328 passengers per minute against an optimal 7.673, with waiting-time variance 84.971.

models.purpose: Keep pre-check passengers off regular points at a measured cost.
models.summary: A penalty term weighted by V is added to the drift. With V = 0.5 the throughput falls to 7.224 and the variance rises to 149.880. The paper states the loss openly: throughput and variance are given up to protect pre-check passengers. Thirteen regular points out of sixteen suit backpressure; eleven suit this algorithm.
